title: Synthetic hotset emulation and KV murmuration adapter
creator: Aisha Navarro
description: Introduce a low-cost background component that emulates tenant hotsets and gently primes both model parameter residency and KV cache entries prior to traffic surges. The approach combines a synthetic hotset generator (small, representative inference traces) with a KV 'murmuration' adapter that issues low-priority cache-touching requests across the fleet. Goal: reduce 99th-percentile cold-start amplification for Dedicated fleets while keeping committed cost and memory churn within SLA budgets.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end synthetic-hotset agent deployed to staging and configurable per-tenant hotset profile
KV murmuration adapter implemented with priority throttling and backpressure aware pacing
Integration with fleet admission controller so prewarm activity counts toward autoscaler target without inflating user-visible capacity metrics
Validated perf run showing >=35% reduction in cold-start P99 tail for staged repro and <=15% increase in baseline memory churn
Docs added to Console about opt-in flags, tenant budgets, and observability metrics (prewarm_tokens, prewarm_failures)
comments: 2026-02-26: Kickoff sync — decided to decouple hotset synthesis from actual customer inputs to avoid PII. We'll use anonymized shard-level access patterns + short prompt templates.
2026-03-01: Prototype run on dedicated-fleet-staging showed initial P99 reduction of ~22% but introduced spiky page faults on older GPU nodes. Raised mitigation ticket to page residency limiter.

2026-03-05: Design review with PM and SRE — agreed on two-mode operation: 'soft-murmur' (continuous low-rate) and 'burst-murmur' (predictive ramp using scheduled traffic forecasts). PM requested per-tenant budget controls in Console.
2026-03-09: PR opened for synthetic agent harness and scheduler: https://github.com/redwood/re-runtime/pull/1422. Added unit tests and a mock KV shim for CI.
2026-03-11: Load test 3 completed. P99 reduction improved to 39% when used with KV prefix caching. Noted cost trade-off: idle GPU memory residency increased ~9% for warmed nodes.
2026-03-12: SRE asked to add circuit-breaker to stop prewarm when node-level memory pressure > 85%. Implemented and pushed to staging branch.
Next steps: finalize console UI for tenant budgets, add tracing spans to link prewarm touches to downstream inference traces for debugging, schedule canary on 2 dedicated clusters.
notes: Rationale: Traditional one-shot weight preloads miss temporal locality introduced by changing prompt distributions. Synthetic emulation allows continuous, low-cost warming that covers short-tailed hotspots.
Trade-offs: Small increase in background memory residency and network egress. Benefit: fewer SLA violations during sudden traffic shifts and improved tail latency for bursty tenants.
Privacy: Synthetic traces must not contain customer content. We use templated prompts + randomization seeded by tenant traffic fingerprints only (no raw text capture).

Operational controls: tenant budget (tokens/sec), cluster-level throttle, memory-pressure circuit-breaker, and a safety fallback that signals autoscaler to spin additional capacity instead of further prewarming when nearing thresholds.
